A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 37 pages, including Appendices A–K. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a complete comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original robustness analyses of LLM arenas and sports datasets, including targeted deletions, bootstrap rankings, random-deletion experiments, and preference case studies.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical analyses and their results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The Bradley–Terry formulation, AMIP-based subset selection, pairwise checks, and exact refitting procedure remain identical in Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chatbot, Vision, Search, Webdev, MT-bench, NBA, and ATP tennis datasets, including the same human-judge and LLM-judge scenarios.

E2.justification: The uniform-at-random deletion comparison in Appendix A.3 and the participating model sets are unchanged. Appendix F reverses the ordering of two existing models without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, preprocessing, tested top-k values, deletion settings, and point-estimate versus bootstrap-ranking procedures are unchanged in Sections 4 and Appendices A and D.

E4.justification: The random-deletion, score-margin, player-involvement, subset-verification, and prompt-response analyses retain the same designs and supporting evidence. The isolated ranking statement revision is reported under E6.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and the same reporting of 100 random-deletion trials in Appendix A. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Appendix F, page 27, reverses the reported top-model transition after dropping two preferences: v3 says GPT-4-0125-preview is replaced by GPT-4-1106-preview; v4 says the reverse. The deletion count, percentages, tables, figures, and remaining results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The robustness definitions, Proposition B.1 and its proof, and the AMIP and logistic-regression derivations in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same methodological contribution and claims about ranking fragility, MT-bench robustness, and human versus LLM judges.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning unusual preferences, narrow score margins, and annotation quality remain unchanged, as do the distinctions from sampling uncertainty and the masking/false-negative limitations.

D1.justification: Hardware and runtime disclosures, dataset identifiers, preprocessing details, qualitative-judge prompt and access description, and technical access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to adversarial leaderboard manipulation and prior data-dropping methods are identical.

P1.justification: Editing is confined to swapping the model names in one Appendix F sentence and updating the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 18 figures, four tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the version/date text and the model-name swap, with no layout revision.

improvement.justification: The revised Appendix F transition better fits its listed GPT-4-0125-preview losses and Figure 3(a)'s original score ordering, improving the coherence of this example. The benefit is limited: Section 4.2 and Appendices E and F.1 retain contradictory ordering statements, while the broader method and evidence are unchanged.
